teaching.hint: Can the contribution of each word be decided once, before considering any query?

solution_outline.decisive_insight: Whether a word qualifies is independent of every query, so a cumulative count can answer static range requests by subtraction.
solution_outline.approach: Mark each word as qualifying or not, build counts for prefixes ending just before every index, then answer inclusive [left,right] by subtracting the prefix before left from the prefix through right.
solution_outline.state_and_invariant: The prefix count at position i equals the number of qualifying words at indices below i. Each query difference therefore includes exactly its requested indices.
solution_outline.correctness: The one-time predicate identifies precisely words with both ends in the vowel set, including a one-letter vowel word. Subtracting the count before left from the count before right+1 cancels all earlier words and leaves every qualifying word in the inclusive interval once.
solution_outline.complexity: O(n + q) time and O(n) auxiliary space for n words and q queries; word-end checks take constant time because words are nonempty.
solution_outline.pitfall: An inclusive right endpoint requires the count through right, while a left endpoint of zero must work without accessing a negative prefix index.

accepted_alternatives: Store the sorted indices of qualifying words and binary-search both query boundaries; this is correct in O(n + q log n) time.
common_wrong_turns: Count words with a vowel at only one end
source_fidelity_notes: Examples were omitted; the vowel set, both-end test, inclusive query bounds, output order, word/query limits, and one-letter behavior were retained.
